claims.statement: Brownsville's City Commission took up the moratorium process at its September 1 meeting.
claims.quote: The Commission considered the process for a temporary moratorium covering data centers, private gaming clubs, automotive quick-lube facilities, event centers, and self-storage facilities while the City evaluates potential regulations.

claims.statement: Commissioners approved a resolution directing the city manager to initiate the process for a temporary ninety-day moratorium.
claims.quote: Commissioners approved a resolution directing the city manager to initiate the process to adopt a temporary 90-day moratorium on high-intensity data processing facilities.
claims.source: MyRGV reporting syndicated by Lower RGV News

claims.statement: City staff said Brownsville's Unified Development Code has no specific data-center regulations.
claims.quote: City staff explained that Brownsville’s Unified Development Code does not currently contain specific regulations addressing data centers.

claims.statement: The proposed process is intended to give the city time to study electricity, water, noise, land use, infrastructure, and economic and fiscal impacts.
claims.quote: The proposed process would give the City time to study issues including electricity and energy use, water consumption, noise, land-use compatibility, infrastructure, and potential economic and fiscal impacts.

claims.statement: The proposal calls for reactivating the Environmental and Conservation Task Force to study data centers and recommend rules.
claims.quote: The proposal also calls for reactivating the City’s Environmental and Conservation Task Force, which would study data center development and provide recommendations to the City Commission.

claims.statement: An initial moratorium may last up to ninety days and may be extended once for another ninety days after further proceedings.
claims.quote: Under state law, an initial moratorium could remain in effect for up to 90 days and could later be extended for another 90 days after additional required proceedings.

claims.statement: City administrators proposed an October 6 hearing, October 13 first reading, and November 17 final vote.
claims.quote: City administrators proposed a schedule that includes a second public hearing on Oct. 6, a first reading of the moratorium ordinance on Oct. 13, and second reading and final vote of the ordinance on Nov. 17.
claims.source: MyRGV reporting syndicated by Lower RGV News

claims.statement: Under the proposed schedule, a moratorium would start November 18 only if the ordinance is approved.
claims.quote: Under the proposed schedule, the data center moratorium would run from Nov. 18 to Feb. 16, 2027 with the option for commissioners to extend it by another 90 days.
claims.source: MyRGV reporting syndicated by Lower RGV News

claims.statement: The City of Brownsville links the complete September 1 meeting video from its official account.
claims.quote: You can view the entire City Commission Meeting by clicking on the following link

claims.statement: The maximum moratorium duration is one hundred eighty days: an initial ninety days plus one possible ninety-day extension.
claims.quote: The moratorium is limited to 90 days. Thereafter, we can extend it for another 90 days. So, the total that we can do a moratorium is 180 days

claims.statement: Brownsville offers online registration for public comments before commission meetings.
claims.quote: Public Comment Registration is now available online. Public Comment Registration Form must be submitted an hour before the scheduled Commission Meeting.

rejected.claim: Brownsville enacted a data-center moratorium on September 1.
rejected.reason: The vote began the process. The ordinance and the moratorium itself are not yet in effect.

rejected.claim: The ninety-day moratorium clock is already running.
rejected.reason: The reported proposed schedule starts it November 18 only if final adoption occurs first.
The city is studying a temporary application pause and permanent regulations, not a categorical ban.

rejected.claim: The proposed October and November dates are guaranteed.
rejected.reason: They are an administrator-proposed schedule and require posted proceedings and later votes.

rejected.claim: A particular Brownsville project consumes a stated amount of electricity or water.
rejected.reason: The withdrawn applicant disclosed no verified operating specifications in the sources used here.

evidence_policy: Status words carry the story. Start-process, proposed schedule, final vote, adopted ordinance and active moratorium are kept separate in every line and every frame.
